g.text: A modern overview of the Land of the Rising Sun
Map: Stylized representation of the Japanese archipelago.

div.style: font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif; font-size: 13.5px; color: #475569; line-height: 1.8; text-align: justify;

foreignObject.div:
Japan is an archipelago in the Pacific Ocean, comprising 6,852 islands. The four largest — Honshu, Hokkaido, Kyushu, and Shikoku — make up about 97% of its land area.
Bordered by the Sea of Japan to the west and the Pacific Ocean to the east, it lies on the "Ring of Fire", experiencing frequent seismic activity. Over 70% of the terrain is mountainous, fostering dense urban populations along coastal plains.
The capital, Tokyo, is the world's most populous metropolitan area, a seamless blend of centuries-old temples and futuristic skyscrapers.

div.style: font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif; font-size: 14px; color: #334155; line-height: 1.7; text-align: justify;

foreignObject.div: As the world's third-largest economy, Japan excels in automotive and electronics innovation. The nation faces complex demographic shifts, including an aging population and a declining birth rate. In response, it leads the world in robotics, AI, and sustainable urban planning. Rooted in Shinto and Buddhist traditions, Japanese culture embraces a philosophy of resilience, harmony ("wa"), and meticulous craftsmanship ("monozukuri"). Today, Japan balances its rich historical identity with a pioneering vision for the future.

div.style: font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif; font-size: 13.5px; color: #475569; line-height: 1.8; text-align: justify;

foreignObject.div:
Japan's nominal GDP has fluctuated over the past decade, peaking at $5.12 trillion in 2019. The services sector dominates, contributing over 70% to the economy, while manufacturing remains globally vital.
Despite this strength, the nation grapples with a debt-to-GDP ratio exceeding 250%, the highest among developed nations. Exports of vehicles, semiconductors, and steel continue to drive economic resilience, even as the yen's valuation shifts.
Recent policy focuses on digital transformation and "Society 5.0" to sustain long-term growth.
